# Tracy fork of dsh-better-sidebar — 0.24.1-tracy.96

`-tracy.96` (27/10/2026, TCH branch `os/tch-opensource-followup`, on top of `.95`). **Dependency security fix only.** `dompurify` `^3.4.16` → `^3.4.17` (GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7, GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr, GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f); the lockfile resolves it, and mermaid's own copy, to 3.4.17. No source change.

`-tracy.95` (27/10/2026, TCH branch `os/tch-opensource-followup`, on top of `.94`). **Test data and comments only, for the public export.** A team member's handle in the mention tests (`tests/thread-mention-parts.spec.ts`, `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx`) and in two source comments became the made-up `@octopal`. No runtime change.

`-tracy.94` (26/10/2026, TCH branch `os/w3-vendor-clean`, on top of `.93`). **Test data only, for the public export.** Real team addresses in `tests/comment-mentions.spec.ts` became fictional `@example.com` ones and the machine path in `tests/mention-intercept.spec.ts` became `/Users/you`. No runtime change.

`-tracy.93` (23/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/sidebar-relative-download`, on top of `.92`, found testing `.92` on dev). **A file link the agent writes in the chat downloads.** The agent names a file it made relative to the conversation's folder (`tracy_business-template.zip`); the side panel opened it as it is and `/sidebar/file` refused every such path `"…" is not an absolute path` (measured on cowork.tracy.site 23/10: 400 JSON for the agent's own template zip) — the very refusal `.92` stopped saving as `file.json`, but the file still never came down. The route now joins a relative path onto the session's cwd before the same workspace fence (`ensureWorkspacePath`), so `../` out of the folder is still 403. Tests: `tests/file-download.spec.ts` (a relative path served; `../secret.zip` refused).

`-tracy.92` (23/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/beta-week-1023`, on top of `.91`, bug B6 of the beta week report 16–23/10). **A download from the side panel is the file, or says why it is not.** A customer asked the agent for a zip of their modified template; the "no preview — download" link in the side panel saved `file.json`: `/sidebar/file?…&download=1` refused the zip (over the 20 MiB `mediaLimit`, the cap the editor DRAWS files under) with its JSON envelope, and the bare `<a download>` saved that envelope as the file. The agent then put the zip in the site's public `images/` folder so the customer could fetch it. Now (1) `?download=1` serves up to `uploadLimit` (128 MiB by default; the editor's own reads keep `mediaLimit`), read whole as before (the archive route already holds up to `ZIP_MAX_BYTES` of one archive), and a refusal names the size and the limit (`too large: 30 MB, the limit is 20 MB`); (2) `src/client/save-download.ts` `saveDownload` fetches first and throws the route's own message, the way `saveArchive` already did, and both the pane (`binary-download.tsx`, the message under the link) and the tree's Download (`FileTree.tsx` `downloadFile`, the action strip) use it. New locale key `downloadFailed` in every locale file. Tests: `tests/file-download.spec.ts`. TCH's site context tells the agent such a file stays outside `.webroot/` (`TAKE_AWAY_LINE`).

`-tracy.91` (15/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/voice-comment`, on top of `.90`, David: voice in the comment popover, "flow y chang" as the chat box's). **The comment popover and the thread card's Reply box get Tracy's microphone — the chat box's own component, drawn here.** The fork imports nothing of Tracy's: TCH `@tracy/dsh-chat-input` puts `{version: 1, Component}` on the dsh page's window under `__TRACY_VOICE_INPUT__` and dispatches `tracy:voice-input-changed` (again when it goes away); `src/client/voice-bridge.ts` listens first and reads after (`useVoiceComponent`, `useSyncExternalStore`), so either bundle may load first, and no global, another version or a non-component draws nothing. The Component is TCH's `VoiceInput` with the operator's switch (`composer-voice-input`), the words and the language hint already bound, taking the props of dsh's `conversation.input.activity` slot; `src/client/CommentVoice.tsx` adapts a `<textarea>` to them (`textDraft`: `captureInsertion` = the caret while the box has focus, else the end of the words; `insertText` replaces exactly its span and only at the revision it was read at, so a box the person typed into refuses and the microphone stops with the words kept; every change moves the revision; `submit` = the box's own Enter action) and wraps it in an error boundary (a microphone that throws is dropped, the box works on, `console.error` with the plugin prefix). `CommentLayer.tsx`: the popover root and the thread card's compose area carry `data-voice-composer` (the microphone's keyboard rules apply inside: Enter finishes the last phrase then presses the box's Enter once, Esc takes the dictated words back out and leaves the box OPEN, typing or Shift+Enter stops it with the words kept); the microphone stands inside the text field like the Reply box's paperclip (the popover: bottom right; the Reply box: top, left of the paperclip; the words kept clear of it through `:has()`), so the foot keeps its width — measured on the local stand, a microphone in the foot wrapped "Note for team" and "Ask Tracy to edit ↵" under the paperclip; listening (`onActiveChange`), its row runs along the field's bottom (`.commentVoiceOn`, the words padded above it) and the paperclip, Delete and the button Enter does not press step aside. The Enter action is the one `useEnterKeys` already pressed (new pick: Ask Tracy, or Note for team for a Viewer; reopened comment: Save; thread: Ask Tracy, or Reply for a Viewer); a send on its way locks the microphone. No locale key is added (the words are Tracy's). Tests: `tests/comment-voice.spec.tsx` (adapter, contract, popover and Reply foot while listening, each Enter action, Viewer, lock, a throwing microphone, an unknown version); TCH `packages/ui/tracy-chat-input/test/voice-bridge.test.mjs` holds the names and version equal on both sides, TCH `test/e2e/voice-comment.test.mjs` runs the real microphone in this adapter.

`-tracy.90` (15/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/ds-templates-local`, asked by the product owner). **The Browser toolbar gets a Publish button and a More (⋯) button right of Comments, driven by Tracy.** Same arrangement as the Design system button (`-tracy.88`): the fork imports nothing of Tracy's and adds no locale key. TCH `@tracy/dsh-my-sites` publishes `tracy:site-toolbar-state` `{siteKey, publish: string|null, more: string|null}` with the words already translated; `src/client/site-toolbar.ts` keeps the latest one per site from module load and sends `tracy:site-toolbar-ask` once when it starts, so a state said before it loaded is said again. `SiteToolbarButtons.tsx`, after the mode bar (so both stay when Edit mode cannot run), draws Publish only when `publish` is a word (Tracy says null while the site's publish state is unknown, the rule of My Sites' row menu) and More only when `more` is; a press (the tab leaves fullscreen first) sends `tracy:site-toolbar-press` `{siteKey, sessionId, action: 'publish'|'more', anchor}`, `anchor` being the pressed button. Tracy opens the site's Publish tab (`tracy:site-publish`) or draws My Sites' own site menu under the button. Publish wears the Comments button's classes (`commentsButton`, compact `commentsButtonIcon`, `LuGlobe`), More the bar's ghost square (`iconButton`, `LuEllipsis`): no colour of their own. Tests: `tests/site-toolbar.spec.tsx`.


`-tracy.89` (12/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/tracy-site-sc3-sidebar`, bug SB-1 of `tasks/todo-bugs-tracy-site.md`). **The agent-opens push socket no longer gives up on a page that was only idle.** `sidebar/use-host-feeds.ts` counted every close toward `FAILURE_LIMIT` (3), opened or not, and never reset the count, although its own comment said "consecutive reconnect failures". Behind Cloudflare an idle WebSocket is dropped after ~2 minutes (measured on cowork.tracy.site 12/10: closes at 132 s and 260 s, each reconnect opened in 2 s), so every session page left open for ~6 minutes logged `[dsh-better-sidebar] agent-opens connection failed; stopping reconnect loop` and stopped receiving the agent's `sidebar_open` requests until a session switch. A socket that opens now resets the count (`onopen`, as `use-dir-watch.ts` already did); three connections in a row that never open still stop the loop with the same error. Tests: `tests/agent-opens-reconnect.spec.tsx` (red without the reset: 3 sockets instead of 7).

`-tracy.89`, second fix (12/10/2026, same branch, PR #1204, bug SEC-2 of `tasks/todo-bugs-tracy-site.md`). **The workspace fence is no longer an existence oracle.** `path-security.ts` `ensureWorkspacePath` ran `realpath` on the target before checking containment, so a seat of site A probing site B's webroot got 400 `fs-error` (ENOENT) for a missing file and 403 `forbidden` for an existing one (measured on cowork.tracy.site 12/10). Both guards now check the path as spelled against the workspace before any I/O on it, and a target that fails to resolve is checked through its nearest resolvable ancestor before its error is reported, so a symlink planted inside the workspace that points into another site gives the same 403 whether the file behind it exists or not; the real-path check after resolution still refuses an escaping symlink. Every refusal names the path the client sent (`path "…" is outside workspace`), never what it resolved to. Inside the workspace a missing file still answers ENOENT; with `workspaceFence` off nothing changes. Tests: `tests/path-security-probe.spec.ts` (3 red before), TCH `scripts/test/seat-isolation-files-tab.test.ts` (SEC-2 case).

`-tracy.88` (11/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/design-system-button`, PR #1134, plan `tasks/ke-hoach-nut-design-system.md`). **The Browser toolbar gets a Design system button, driven by Tracy.** Same arrangement as the Undo button (`-tracy.78`): the fork imports nothing of Tracy's and adds no locale key. TCH `@tracy/dsh-design-inspiration` publishes `tracy:design-system-toolbar-state` `{siteKey, state: 'ready'|'off'|'hidden', text: {label, tooltip}}` with the words already translated; `src/client/design-system-toolbar.ts` keeps the latest one per site from module load. `DesignSystemToolbarButton.tsx`, after the mode bar (so it stays when Edit mode cannot run), draws nothing without a state or on `hidden`; `ready` sends `tracy:design-system-toolbar-press` `{siteKey, sessionId}` (the tab leaves fullscreen first) and Tracy opens the site's design-system panel; `off` is inert through `aria-disabled` so its tooltip still says why. Compact toolbar: the icon alone (`LuPalette`), named by `aria-label`. Tests: `tests/design-system-toolbar.spec.tsx`. (Numbered `-tracy.87` on the branch; develop published its own `-tracy.87` first, so this is `-tracy.88`.)

`-tracy.87` (11/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/vendor-deps-advisories`). **Dependencies with published security advisories lifted to their first fixed release of the same major line; no code change.** `dompurify` ^3.4.16 (direct); `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `overrides` lift `undici` 7.29.1, `source-map-js` 1.2.2 and `brace-expansion` 2.1.7 / 5.0.12, all reached only through jsdom and eslint (tests and lint). Left: `katex` (0.16 → 0.18 is a major upgrade, low severity, reached through mermaid).

`-tracy.86` (10/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/account-menu-followups--mobile`). **A thread card no longer opens with its newest message's author line hidden above the list.** Measured on dev 09/10: a one-message card "On body" (an element taller than the frame, so `threadCardMaxHeight` caps the card to `THREAD_CARD_MIN`, 160 px) kept ~53 px of list for a ~70 px message; the list was aimed at its end (`scrollTop = scrollHeight`), so the face and the author line sat above the list's top edge. `ThreadCard` now aims at `newestTop()` (`client/CommentLayer.tsx`): the list's end, unless the newest message is taller than the list — then that message's top. Tests: `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx` ("the newest message taller than the list").

`-tracy.85` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/account-menu-debts--files`, PR #1094). **A seat's Files tab no longer asks for `git.status`.** dsh-passwords keeps every `/sidebar/api/git.*` route owner-only, and it must: this plugin spawns `git` in the host's one dsh process (not in the site's web container, TCH ADR 0014), and `git status` runs commands a repository's own `.git/config` names (`core.fsmonitor`), a file a seat with `fs.write` can author — measured: `status()` of `src/git.ts` on a repo whose `.git/config` sets `core.fsmonitor` ran that command. `-tracy.10`'s rule still cost one 403 per tree slot (two console errors on the `acm` stand). dsh-passwords now marks a seat's page (`globalThis.__TRACY_SIDEBAR_GIT__ = "off"`, its S17); `useGitStatus` (`client/ui/git-status.ts` `gitStatusTurnedOff`) never asks on such a page and reports no error, so the tree renders without git badges. Without the flag nothing changes. Tests: `tests/git-status-forbidden.spec.tsx` ("never asks on a page the gate marked git-off").

Same `-tracy.85` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/account-menu-debts--gitsafe`, PR #1094). **No git call of the fork can run a program the repository names.** `src/git.ts` runs git in the host's one dsh process on site folders a customer's agent can write, and git runs what `.git/config` (and anything it includes), `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/attributes` and `.git/hooks` name: `core.fsmonitor` (measured: `status()` ran it), clean/smudge/process filters (`status`, `diff`, `add`, `checkout`), `diff.<driver>.textconv`/`command` and `diff.external`, merge drivers (`cherry-pick`, `revert`), every hook (`commit`, `checkout`), `gpg.program` with `commit.gpgSign`/`log.showSignature`, pagers, editors, credential helpers, and a submodule's own config. Every repository command now goes through `safeGit`, which never lets git read the repository's config: it builds a private common directory (`GIT_COMMON_DIR`, a temp dir removed after the call) whose `config` holds only a whitelist of inert keys (`core.repositoryformatversion`, `filemode`, `symlinks`, `ignorecase`, `precomposeunicode`, `autocrlf`, `eol`, `safecrlf`, `checkstat`, `trustctime`, `logallrefupdates`, `extensions.objectformat`/`refstorage`; plain values only) read from a snapshot of the real file (`git config --file … --no-includes`), and whose `objects`, `refs`, `packed-refs`, `logs`, `worktrees`, `shallow`, `reftable` and `info/exclude` are symlinks to the real ones; no `hooks`, no `info/attributes`, no `config.worktree`. Because git reads the snapshot, a config rewritten between our read and git's changes nothing (enumerating driver names and overriding each with `-c` would lose that race). Second layer on every call, including `probeGit` (the only path that sees the real repository: `rev-parse` discovery and `worktree list`, which read no index, work-tree file or attribute): command-line `-c` overrides, which outrank every config file and include, for each fixed-name key (`core.fsmonitor=false`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `core.pager=cat`, editors `:`, empty `core.askPass`/`credential.helper`/`diff.external`, signing off, `gc.auto=0`, `maintenance.auto=false`, `submodule.recurse=false`, `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all`, `protocol.allow=never`), an environment with none of dsh's own `GIT_*` plus `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`/`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and flags `--no-textconv` (diff, show), `--ignore-submodules=all` (status, diff), `commit --no-verify`. What the panels lose: a repository-local `user.name`/`email` (commits use the global identity, as the header always said), textconv'd diffs, submodule entries in status/diff, and per-worktree config. System and global config still apply: they are the operator's. Measured cost: `status()` on the TCH tree 739 ms vs 726 ms before. The symlinks need a POSIX host (Linux image, macOS desktop). Tests: `tests/git-safe.spec.ts` (one planted `touch` per vector through the real exported functions, marker absent and panel data correct; plus a source test that `src/` spawns git from exactly one place, `spawnGit`, called only by `probeGit`, `readSafeConfig`, `safeGit`), `tests/git-spawn.spec.ts` updated to the new argument shape. **Same entry: git discovery never leaves the session workspace.** Every exported git function takes the session WORKSPACE (index.ts `sessionScopeOf`, the same root `sessionCwdOf` fences client cwds on; defaults to `cwd`), and `openRepo` refuses (`forbidden`, 403), on read and write routes alike, unless the work tree, the git dir and the common dir all resolve (realpath, symlinks followed) inside it. Before git is asked anything, `checkGitEntry` walks from cwd up to the workspace to the `.git` discovery would use and checks where a `.git` pointer file (`gitdir:`), a `.git` symlink or a linked worktree's `commondir` lead; after `rev-parse`, `core.worktree` is caught by the work-tree check; every symlink directly inside the git/common dir (`objects`, `refs`, `index`…) and every object alternate must lead inside too (`http-alternates` is refused). Discovery probes run with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` = the workspace's parent, so a repository ABOVE the workspace is never found (the panel says "not a git repository"); a refusal is never swallowed into the child-repository scan. `worktrees` lists only checkouts inside the workspace and `resolveWorktree` refuses any other (`forbidden`). Gone with it: upstream's "session in a subdirectory of a larger repository" (smoke `git.diff …session in a subdirectory` now asserts the refusal; the already-red smoke `fs.read resolves repo-relative paths` tests the same gone behaviour). Residual: a path swapped for a symlink between the check and git's use (milliseconds) is not caught; only running git in the site's container closes that. Tests: `tests/git-fence.spec.ts` (pointer file, `.git` symlink, `core.worktree`, `commondir`, alternates, symlinked `refs`, ancestor repository, outside linked worktree: each refused with a victim repository outside fingerprinted unchanged through status/diff/log/branches/worktrees/stage/discard/commit/checkout; a normal repository, a linked worktree inside and a nested cwd still served; one route-level case through `/sidebar/api`), `tests/git-worktree.spec.ts`, `tests/smoke.spec.ts` and `tests/git-spawn.spec.ts` given an explicit workspace.

`-tracy.84` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/account-menu--fork`, plan `tasks/todo-account-menu.md` C6; first numbered `.83`, renumbered on top of `.83` when the Files fix reached develop first). **Every person the fork draws wears the face the server sent, photo included, through one renderer.** New `src/client/face.tsx` mirrors TCH `packages/core/tracy-core/src/team/face.tsx` (copied, not imported: the fork depends on no `@tracy/*`): `PersonFace` `{initial, color, avatarUrl}`, `NEUTRAL_FACE_COLOUR` (`var(--muted-foreground, #94a3b8)`), `fallbackInitial` (the server `personFace` letter rule: first code point of the name, else the email, upper case, `?`) and `Face` (the photo when `avatarUrl`, a photo that fails to load gives way to the letter; round; white letter at 45% of the size, weight 600; `cornerShape: round`; `fill` takes the parent's box and corners). `bubbleFace` now returns that `PersonFace` — the author's `initial`/`color`/`avatarUrl` as sent (no more upper-casing or re-cutting of the server's letter), the viewer's `/auth/me` face for a pending comment, the neutral grey where the server sent no colour, `fallbackInitial` only where it sent no letter. `AvatarPin` (inside its teardrop), the thread card's author and the `@` picker row (`/comments/people`, which kept `avatarUrl` but never drew it) all draw `Face`. Gone: `letterOf`, `BubbleFace`, `NO_FACE_COLOUR` (was `#737373`; a no-face bubble now takes TCH's neutral) and the picker's email-only letter fallback. A lost block's grey pin (`GHOST_PIN_COLOUR`) keeps its grey and letter and shows no photo. Tests: `tests/face.spec.tsx` (letter, photo, broken photo, neutral, letter rule), `tests/comment-store.spec.ts` (`bubbleFace` from server data), `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx` (pin, card and picker draw the photo; grey pin does not), `tests/comment-mentions.spec.ts` (`readPeople` keeps the face, name-first fallback).

`-tracy.83` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/sidebar-files-new-session`, first numbered `.81` on 08/10/2026 and renumbered on top of `.82` when `.81`/`.82` reached develop first). **The Files tab works on a conversation made with New session, without a reload.** A New session's list summary carries no `cwd` until the page reloads. The shell Sidebar already asked the host (`session.cwd`) for it, but the native tab body (where Files is drawn when DSH hosts the tabs) read the summary only, so Files got `scope.cwd === undefined`, drew "Select a conversation to use the sidebar" and never listed the tree. The fallback moves into one hook, `session-cwd.ts` `useSessionCwd`, that both the shell Sidebar and `NativeTabBody` read; an answer about another session never stands in for this one's. Tests: `tests/native-body-session-cwd.spec.tsx`.

`-tracy.82` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/add-site-responsive-my-sites-scroll`, on top of `.81`). **A descriptor may declare `maxWidth` (px), the widest the right panel may be while its tab is active.** `native/index.ts` forwards it to DSH's native tab type (`SidebarRightTabDefinition.maxWidth`, dsh `0.2.0-rc.2-tracy.31`), exactly as `preferredWidth` (`-tracy.19`). DSH then caps the normal panel at that width on frames of 768px or more: a divider drag cannot widen it past the ceiling, a wider panel shrinks to it and gets the user's width back on another tab, and the fullscreen switch and command are off (a recorded fullscreen mode is drawn as a normal panel and comes back on another tab). TCH Add site declares 600px (`FORM_PANEL_WIDTH`). No test here: the field is copied as-is, and the rule is tested in dsh (`ui-layout/tests/columns.client.spec.ts`, `app-frame.client.spec.tsx`, `ui-sidebar-right/tests/seat.client.spec.tsx`). **Same version: the browser tab's site switcher passes `collisionAvoidance` to DSH's `Menu`** (`BrowserTabTitle.tsx`). Without it the per-site submenu (Live Edit, Settings, Team, Site changes) kept the legacy CSS placement, its bottom on the row's bottom and growing upward, so on rows near the top of the window it rose past the viewport (measured on cowork.tracy.site 09/10: 35px above for the first row, 11px for the second, Live Edit cut off). With it the submenu starts at its row and is clamped inside the viewport. Test: `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx` "places the per-site submenu from its row down…" (red without the prop).

`-tracy.81` (09/10/2026, TCH branch `feat/desktop-window-shell`, plan `tasks/todo-desktop-window-shell.md`, on top of `.80`). **The Browser tab's "Open externally" and "Open in browser" open the system browser in the Tracy desktop app too.** The app's window now routes the links it is asked to open (a page of the site on screen opens in this very Browser tab), so `window.open` from these two buttons would have come straight back into the tab. They now call `openExternally(url)` (`src/client/open-externally.ts`): with the app's bridge (`globalThis.tracyDesktop.links.openExternal`, exposed by the app's preload to its own top frame only) it asks the app for the system browser; anywhere else it is upstream's `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')`, so the web is unchanged. No other `window.open` of the fork changes. Tests: `tests/open-externally.spec.ts`.

`-tracy.80` (08/10/2026, TCH #1036 branch `fix/viewer-edit-toggle`, on top of `.79`). **A Viewer seat comments in Edit mode but is never offered "Ask Tracy to edit".** TCH ADR 0028: a Viewer may comment, the agent is read-only for them. The fork imports nothing of Tracy's: TCH `@tracy/dsh-chat-input` keeps `<html data-tracy-seat-viewer>` while the seat's role on the site is `viewer`, and the new `src/client/seat-viewer.ts` (`isSeatViewer`, `useSeatViewer`, a `MutationObserver` on that one attribute, so a role read late still applies) only reads it. Edit mode stays for a Viewer (it is how they pin comments). `CommentLayer.tsx`: in `CommentPopover` a Viewer gets no "Ask Tracy to edit" (new pick, reopened comment and the lost-element foot); "Note for team" (or "Save") is the primary `commentSend` button and Enter presses it; the pointing hint reads `editHintViewer` ("Click any block to leave a note", + "· Esc to stop"), new key in all 22 dictionaries, each cut from that language's own `editHint`. Editors and Owners (no attribute) are unchanged. In a thread card (the reply box under a comment) a Viewer gets no "Ask Tracy to edit" either: "Reply" is primary and takes Enter, and the lost-element foot adds instead of sending. Tests: `tests/seat-viewer.spec.tsx`.

- **tracy.79 (addendum):** removed the red `fail` diagnostic strip pinned to the page (`src/client/index.tsx`); errors now go only to `console.error` with the plugin prefix — a Tracy page is a page the customer sees (web + desktop app). Test `tests/no-diagnostic-strip.spec.ts`. (08/10/2026)


`-tracy.79` (08/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/sidebar-relist-inactive-context`, reported by the product owner in the desktop app, on top of `.78`). **A re-sync that lands while DSH's tab registry unloads no longer pins a red error strip.** DSH's `sidebarRightTabs` registry adds every type as an effect on its own fiber (`ui-sidebar-right`) and withdraws the service last, so while the host unloads (client graph reload, dsh restarting behind the desktop app) the native surface still holds a registry cordis refuses effects on. A sync in that window — Tracy's `followTabPolicy` disposer resetting the tab policy, which re-lists Files — threw `cannot create effect on inactive context`, and `reportFailure` drew it as "[dsh-better-sidebar] native relist files error: …" in the client's diagnostic strip (`src/client/index.tsx` `fail`). `src/client/native/index.ts`: every registration step goes through `attempt`, which recognises cordis's `INACTIVE_EFFECT` code (matched by `code`, so the bundle carries no second cordis), stays silent and stops that closure's syncs (`ctx.inject` re-runs with the next registry); any other refusal is still reported. Tests: `tests/native-host-teardown.spec.ts` (real cordis fiber + the fork's real `SidebarRightTabRegistry`).

`-tracy.78` (06/10/2026, TCH #957 `feat/undo-toolbar-sync`, contract `tasks/undo-change/toolbar-contract.md`, on top of `.77`). **The Browser toolbar gets an Undo button for the conversation's last request, driven by Tracy.** The fork imports nothing of Tracy's: tracy-chat-input publishes `tracy:undo-toolbar-state` `{sessionId, siteKey, state: 'ready'|'off'|'blocked'|'working'|'hidden', text, toast}` with every word already translated, and `undo-toolbar.ts` keeps the latest one per session from module load (a state said before the tab mounts is not lost). `UndoToolbarButton.tsx`, before the mode bar, draws nothing without a state or on `hidden`; `ready` opens a confirm card (`AnchoredPopover`, which gains an optional `label` for its dialog name) whose Undo sends `tracy:undo-toolbar-press` `{sessionId, action: 'confirm'}`; `blocked` draws a warning dot and a card whose action sends `action: 'open-changes'` (the tab leaves fullscreen first); `off` and `working` are inert through `aria-disabled` so their tooltip still explains; a state carrying `toast` shows the notice once per state object for 6 s. No locale key is added; no Redo, no shortcut. Tests: `tests/undo-toolbar.spec.tsx`.

`-tracy.77` (06/10/2026, TCH #957 `fix/undo-preview-reload`, measured on cowork.tracy.site, on top of `.76`). **An undo always reloads the site preview, even within a minute of the turn's end.** TCH `tracy-chat-input`'s turn undo card asks every Browser tab on the site to reload after an undo (`reloadTab`), and `refreshStep` took that request inside the turn's absorb window (`ABSORB_MS`, 60 s) for the turn's own late request: the site was undone but the preview showed the old page until a manual refresh. `reloadTab` gains the documented mode `'undo'` (a full refresh); `BrowserView` maps it to `fresh: true` on the `reload-request` event, which skips the absorb branch without spending the slot, so the turn's own late request is still absorbed. At work, hidden and open-comment-box rules are unchanged. Tests: `tests/refresh-progress.spec.ts` ("an undo asked from the chat's undo card").

`-tracy.76` (05/10/2026, TCH branch `fix/thread-mention-colour`, on top of `.75`). **A thread card draws @mentions in the brand colour, like the chat column's Comments list.** The thread popover printed each message as plain text, so "@octopal @anhvp.ecom" read in white there while the list (TCH `tracy-chat-input` `textParts`) showed them in terracotta. `comment-mentions.ts` gains `mentionParts` (the list's rule: a mention starts at the beginning or after a space and is never an e-mail address) and `CommentLayer` renders the parts with `.threadMention`. Tests: `tests/thread-mention-parts.spec.ts`.

`-tracy.75` (05/10/2026, TCH PR #899 `fix/rename-comment-ui-e2e-0410`, e2e dev run E7.2c; on top of `.74` from TCH PR #891). **A plugin's `updateTab({ meta: { url } })` on a native Browser tab now sticks.** `NativeTabBody` calls `records.ensure` on every render with the same navigation seed, and `ensure` wrote that seed's `url` back into `meta.url` each time — so the record change an `updateTab` makes re-rendered the body and undid itself in the same pass. After a site rename, tracy-tab-link (#818) moved the Browser tab to the new host; the chip took the new title, but the record, the address bar and the frame snapped back to the old host until a page reload (and on WordPress the old-host page then loaded fonts/modules from the new host, CORS-blocked). The record now keeps the seed it last applied (`View.seedUrl`); only a different seed is a navigation. Tests: `tests/native-surface.spec.ts` ("keeps an address a plugin wrote over the url seed…").

`-tracy.74` (05/10/2026, TCH follow-up of PR #685, measured on the `tracy-rc2` stand). **An empty Browser tab in a site workspace starts on the site.** The bottom workbench's `+` opens `tracy:browser` with no address (`Sidebar.tsx` `onNewTab` passes no `url`), which showed the start screen — still worded "(sandbox mode)" from upstream's sandbox tab. `BrowserView` now asks the page's `/api/sites` once (`siteHomeOf`, cached like `siteDomains`) and navigates the empty tab to the site's `copyUrl`; outside a site workspace the start screen stays. `browserStart` loses its sandbox parenthetical in every language (Tracy's tab frames the site without a sandbox). Tests: `tests/tracy-browser-home.spec.tsx`.

`-tracy.73` (04/10/2026, TCH PR #685 `chore/upgrade-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2-impl`, measured on the `tracy-rc2` stand). **A seat's Tasks page stops asking `workflows.list` after one 403.** v0.24.1's `useWorkflowRuns` (`SubagentView.tsx`) polled every `TELEMETRY_POLL_MS` with no refusal memory, and dsh-passwords keeps `workflows.list` to the owner: 144 × 403 in ten minutes on one seat page. Same rule as `useSubagentLive` (`-tracy.10`): a 403 ends the poll for that root, any other failure keeps retrying. Tests: `tests/subagent-live-polling.spec.tsx` ("workflow poll stops on a 403").

`-tracy.72` (04/10/2026, TCH PR #685 `chore/upgrade-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2-impl`, plan `tasks/todo-dsh-core-0-2-0.md`). **The fork moves from upstream `v0.21.1` to upstream `v0.24.1` (DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`), carrying every Tracy entry below.** This is the merge of two lines: the upgrade branch of 01/10 (upstream `v0.24.1` + the Tracy subtree at `-tracy.38`, with the workspace fence re-plugged into upstream's new routes — its two entries follow) and `develop`'s `-tracy.39`…`-tracy.71` (comments, badge chip, Spanish, site names, keepLast). Conflicts were four source files: `native/index.ts` (upstream's slot-registration rollback plus the `ctx` the badge chip reads), `native/tab-adapter.tsx` (imports), `service.ts` (`SIDEBAR_SERVICE_VERSION`) and `sidebar.module.css` (`.commentAvatarPin`: `develop`'s newer pin design kept). DSH peer ranges are `^0.2.0-rc.1`; TCH's eleven consumers pin `>=0.24.1-tracy.1 <0.24.1`. Measurements: `tasks/evidence/dsh-0-2-0-rc-2/`.
  - *(was `-tracy.40` on the upgrade branch, 01/10/2026 — the number was reused on `develop` by a different change)* Let the `tracy:browser` descriptor register a native guide entry. Tracy's `launch-browser` tab policy still hides it by default and lists it only when the operator enables the switch. TCH also adds the native `files` kind to the `launch-files` switch and launcher list; the editor descriptor alone cannot appear in the native + menu because its guide row belongs to `files`. The local `tracy-rc2` stand exposed both mismatches: after enabling Browser and Files in `/ops`, + still listed only Side Chat.
  - *(was `-tracy.39` on the upgrade branch, 01/10/2026 — the number was reused on `develop` by a different change)* Rebased the fork from upstream `v0.21.1` plus the Tracy subtree onto upstream `v0.24.1`, carrying the host jobs client, workflow/team/task views, and the new filesystem UI. Kept Tracy's `available`-aware native guide and tab policy, Browser `keepMounted`/site navigation, fail-closed workspace fence, and session-owned legacy jobs fence. The host client jobs service replaces the sidebar's 3-second roster poll and model-cursor output replay; the gateway still must authorize `job/list` and `job/follow` per granted session, and deny foreign `job/kill` before this is used on a stand. Changes in `fs-operations.ts`, `fs-tree.ts`, `path-security.ts`, and route tests restore realpath containment where upstream removed it. DSH peer ranges are `^0.2.0-rc.1`; exact DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` development pins match this integration. Build: `pnpm build`; validation: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (three existing hook warnings), 170 test files / 2,296 passed / 9 skipped with `vitest --maxWorkers=1`.

`-tracy.71` (04/10/2026, TCH #858 follow-up `feat/site-changes-badge-count`, measured on the `badge` stand). **A native chip draws its type's badge, and a plugin can say the value moved.** `TabDescriptor.badge` was read only by the workbench strip's `tabBadgeOf` (`Sidebar.tsx` → `TabBar.tsx`), which draws no right column when dsh hosts the tabs (0.1.5+): the native chip (`NativeTabTitle`, `native/tab-adapter.tsx`) drew glyph and title alone, so TCH's Site changes count on the `tracy:changes` tab never appeared. The chip now reads `descriptor.badge(ctx, scope, state)` too (`nativeTabBadge`; the title slot's injection hands it `ctx`), drawn with the strip's own pill (`css.tabBadge`) and the shared `tabBadgeText` (99+ cap; null/''/undefined draw nothing; a throw is logged and draws nothing). A badge is pulled on render only, so a value that moves for a reason the side card cannot see (a store's poll, another person's work) showed late at best: `BetterSidebarService.invalidateTabBadges()` (with `subscribeTabBadges` / `tabBadgeRevision`, feature `tabBadgeInvalidation`) lets the registrant say so, and every chip and the strip re-read their badges. Tests: `tests/native-surface.spec.ts` ("a native chip draws the descriptor badge and re-draws it when a plugin invalidates badges"), `tests/service.spec.ts` (the feature; an invalidation bumps the revision and tells the subscribers).

`-tracy.70` (04/10/2026, TCH `feat/comment-unread-dot`, decided by the product owner). **"Comments N" draws the site's open comments in grey, and a terracotta dot while this person has unread ones.** tracy-chat-input's `tracy:comment-unread` now carries `{count, open}` — `count` the unread open threads as before (null until the read marks are in), `open` every open thread of the site, all authors — and is sent whenever either changes; `tracy:comment-unread-state` is answered with both. `comment-store.ts` replaces `readUnreadCount`/`askUnreadCount` with `readCommentsBadge`/`askCommentsBadge`, which return a `CommentsBadge` `{open, unread}`: a detail with an `open` field draws `open` as the number (`open: 0` is no number, never a fallback to `count`) and `count` as the dot; a detail without it (an older chat input) draws `count` as the number with no dot, as `-tracy.69` did. `CommentsButton` takes `open` and `unread` instead of `count`: the badge (`.commentsCount`) turns grey (`--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2` / `--dsw-alias-label-tertiary`, Tracy's `--muted` / `--muted-foreground`) and, while `unread` is above 0, wears `data-dot` (a 7 px `::after` dot of `--dsw-alias-brand-primary`, ringed in `--dsw-alias-bg-base`) with the tooltip "N unread"; the button's name becomes "Comments, N, M unread". `unread` null or 0 draws no dot and no words. One new key `commentsUnread` (`{count} unread`) in every dictionary. Tests: `tests/comment-store.spec.ts` (`readCommentsBadge`, `askCommentsBadge`), `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx` (the dot on the button and on the compact corner badge), `tests/tracy-browser-toolbar.spec.tsx` (the open number moves when only `open` changes, the dot when only `count` does, a late toolbar asks `-state`, an older chat input still draws its count).

`-tracy.69` (04/10/2026, TCH `feat/team-badge-count`, decided by the product owner after a Codex review). **A comment author's face comes from the server; the fork hashes nothing.** `comment-store.ts` loses `AUTHOR_COLOURS`, `authorColor` and `authorColours` (the FNV-1a of the account id and the namesake colour shift): `CommentAuthor` now carries `initial`, `color` and `avatarUrl` exactly as `GET /api/sites/:key/comments` sends them (tracy-web's one `personFace` helper, shared with `/api/team` and `/auth/me`), and `AvatarPin`, the thread card and `commentListDetail` (`tracy:comment-list` `author`) read those fields. A comment the server has not answered yet has no `author`: its pin wears the viewer's own face, read once per tab through the new `CommentApi.me()` (`GET /auth/me` `face`, kept as `CommentMode.viewerFace`), or the neutral `NO_FACE_COLOUR` (= `GHOST_PIN_COLOUR`) with no letter until it arrives. Two namesakes may now share a colour; the name tells them apart. Tests: `tests/comment-store.spec.ts` (the list detail copies the server's face; namesakes keep the server's colour), `tests/comment-people-controller.spec.tsx` (a pending comment's pin: the viewer's face, then the server's), `tests/comment-api.spec.ts` (`me()`).

`-tracy.68` (04/10/2026, TCH spec #809 case C1, picker U6). **`@` in a comment box lists the site's people, and a pick names that account.** Typing `@` in the new-comment popover, the edit popover or the thread card's reply box lists the people holding a live seat on the site (`GET /api/sites/:key/comments/people`, `CommentApi.people`), each with avatar (pin colour, initial), name, address and role, under them "Only people with a seat on this site". ↑/↓, Enter/Tab picks, Esc closes the list only (the box keeps its words), a click picks. A pick writes `@handle ` (first name word, else the address before `@`, only characters the chat column's mention colouring takes) and the controller remembers that account id for the box; the POST/PATCH carries `mentions: [id…]` for each pick whose `@handle` the words still carry, so a typed `@name` nobody picked stays plain text. An edit sends the whole list (the stored mentions the words still name, as the roster knows them, plus new picks), or leaves it out when the roster could not be read. The list is drawn in flow under the field (the popover and the card scroll inside). New: `comment-mentions.ts` (pure rules), `CommentMentionPicker.tsx`; three keys `mentionPeople`, `mentionOnlySeats`, `mentionNoMatch` in every dictionary. Tests: `tests/comment-mentions.spec.ts`, `tests/comment-people-controller.spec.tsx` ("the @ picker names people by account"), `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx` ("the @ picker under a comment box").

`-tracy.67` (04/10/2026, TCH `fix/comment-card-tracy-done`, wording decided after TCH #822, ADR 0025). **A thread Tracy resolved says so in the Comments list's own words.** The resolved pill on the thread card had "Resolved by Tracy" as its tooltip while the Comments tab tags the same comment "Tracy marked this done". `comment-api.ts` `commentFromServer` keeps the server's `resolvedByTracy: true` on a resolved row as `Comment.resolvedByTracy` (dropped on reopen, `comment-store.ts` `openAgain`); `CommentLayer.tsx` `ThreadHead` then titles the pill `commentDoneByTracy` instead of `commentResolvedBy`. A person's resolve is unchanged. New copy `commentDoneByTracy` in all 21 dictionaries; en, vi, de, es, fr, it, nl and zh reuse TCH `tracy-chat-input`'s `comments.tag.tracy` word for word. Tests: `tests/comment-api.spec.ts` (`resolvedByTracy`), `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx` (the pill's tooltip, the dictionary check), `tests/comment-store.spec.ts` (a reply drops it).

`-tracy.66` (03/10/2026, TCH `feat/browser-tab-pinned`, decided by the product owner). **The site preview's last tab stays in its column in a site workspace.** The Browser tab is the site workspace's own page (Edit and Comments live in it), and a person could close it with ✕ and land on an empty "Click + to start" column. `TabDescriptor.keepLast?: () => boolean` is passed through `native/index.ts` `registerType` to dsh's `SidebarRightTabDefinition.keepLast` (dsh `0.1.7-rc.2-tracy.16`), which hides ✕ and menu Close on a column's last tab of that kind and makes `page.close` collapse the column instead. `tracyBrowserTab()` declares it while `siteKeyOfBase(document.baseURI)` names a site — the creation workspace (`/new/`) keeps nothing. A second Browser tab still closes; the column still collapses. Tests: `tests/native-surface.spec.ts` ("the site preview keeps its last tab in a site workspace"). **A renamed site shows its new name** (TCH #818, reported by the product owner on the stand): a rename keeps `siteKey` and puts the new name in the `/api/sites` row's `displayName`, older ones in `aliases`; the chip and the site menu printed `siteKey` (the old address), and the page's own path — the current name — was compared with row keys, so picking the open site opened it again in a new window. `site-name.ts`: `siteNameOf` (`displayName`, else the key) labels chip and menu; `siteNamed` finds the page's site by key, current name or alias. Tests: `tests/site-name.spec.ts`, `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx` ("shows a renamed site by its new name").

`-tracy.65` (03/10/2026, TCH `feat/retire-release-for-backup`, ADR 0024 follow-up). **The Browser tab's site menu opens Site changes instead of the retired History.** Each site's submenu read Live Edit · Settings · Team · History, and History opened `tracy:history`, a type TCH locked off when Backup took over from releases (ADR 0024): on the same site the open was refused with only a console warning, on another site a new window opened on `?tab=tracy:history` and showed nothing. The row is now **Site changes** (key `browserSiteChanges`, was `browserSiteHistory`, in `locales.ts` zh + en and every `locales-<lang>.ts`; Tracy's eight languages use the words of its own Site changes tab) with the checklist glyph (`VscChecklist`, the tab's own `ListChecks`), and opens `tracy:changes`: in the current window for the site on screen (`openLocal`), as `/<site>/?tab=tracy:changes&site=<site>` in a new window for another site. TCH retires `tracy:releases` and `tracy:history` in the same change and redirects both to `tracy:changes` (deep links and saved layouts). Tests: `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx` (the site menu rows and their destinations).

`-tracy.64` (03/10/2026, TCH spec #730, measured on cowork.tracy.site). **A tab opened through `openTab` follows a language switch too.** `service.openTab` wrote the type's own label into the native navigation params as `title` even when the caller named none, and the tab adapter reads a params title as "named by a plugin": the record was minted `titled`, and once the body unmounted (another tab picked) the chip fell back to the host's stored title, the label in the language the tab was first opened in. Seen: Team opened by a `?tab=` link showed "Đội" in a zh interface after leaving it, "Add site" stayed English in zh/it/fr. Now only a title the caller or the descriptor's factory chose rides the params (`chosenTitle`), and a chip with no record shows a params title before the host's stored copy. Tests: `tests/native-surface.spec.ts` ("a page tab opened through openTab follows a language switch after its body unmounts", "a tab whose navigation names its own title shows that title before its body mounts").

`-tracy.63` (02/10/2026, TCH spec #730 / issue #765). **A comment's "not sent" line follows the interface language.** When a send leaves out a file (over the size cap, past the file cap, or unreadable), `comment-attachments.ts` `notSentLine` appended `(<file> not sent: too large)` in English to the comment's words in every language. It now goes through the side card's own `t()`: three keys `commentNotSentTooLarge`, `commentNotSentTooMany`, `commentNotSentUnreadable` (`{name}` hole) in `locales.ts` (zh, en) and every `locales-<lang>.ts` (the build's key-set check requires all of them). Tests: `tests/comment-attachments.spec.ts` ("the line a send adds for a file that could not go").

`-tracy.62` (02/10/2026, TCH spec #730 / tickets #751 #752). **Native Spanish wording in the side card.** A native-speaker review of `src/client/locales-es.ts` replaced the English product words the first pass kept (workspace, commit…) with the Spanish ones the rest of the `es` interface uses ("espacio de trabajo", "confirmación"), and fixed two meanings: the discard warning names the working tree ("árbol de trabajo"), and the revert description uses the subjunctive for a commit not yet made ("que revierta"). 23 values changed, no key added or removed; code untouched.

`-tracy.61` (02/10/2026, TCH spec #730 / ticket #740 follow-up, measured on cowork.tracy.site). **A restored tab nobody opened yet follows a language switch too.** tracy.60 drew the type label fresh only for a tab that HAS a record, but a record is minted when a tab's body first mounts; a tab restored from the saved layout and never clicked (Site changes, Team beside the active Browser tab) had none, so its chip kept the host's stored "Site changes" / "Team" in a Spanish interface. With no record, `NativeTabTitle` now reads the type label fresh unless the tab is an editor/diff tab or its navigation carries its own `title`, `path` or `diff`. `-tracy.60` (02/10/2026, TCH spec #730 / ticket #740). **The side card speaks Spanish.** Tracy adds `es` itself (`@tracy/dsh-tracy-locales` `languages.json`), and with no better-locale override store the sidebar reads its own dictionary for the active language from the lazy `locale` chunk; that chunk had 19 languages and no Spanish, so an `es` interface kept the toolbar's Edit / Comments and every side-card label in English. `locales-es.ts` (554 keys, the same key set as zh, enforced by `chunks/locale.tsx` `checked`) joins `localeDicts`. Wording: formal usted; workspace and skill kept in English as on Tracy's Spanish dsh screens. **An open tab follows a language switch** (`native/tab-adapter.tsx`): the host stores a tab's title as a string when it opens, so every open tab kept the language it was opened in. A record now remembers whether its title came from somewhere other than the type's label (`View.titled`: a navigation seed, a mint, or `updateTab({ title })`); while it did not, and the tab is not bound to a file (`path`/`diff`), `NativeTabTitle` draws `descriptor.title()` fresh, re-rendering on `<html lang>` changes and on the sidebar's own dictionary revision. Titles a plugin sets stay the plugin's to rename (TCH's plugins rebuild theirs on a language switch). Tests: `tests/native-surface.spec.ts` ("an open tab follows a language switch"), `tests/locales.spec.ts` (22 dictionaries).

`-tracy.59` (02/10/2026, TCH `fix/comment-read-on-any-open`, the product owner's decision). **The toolbar's "Comments N" is this person's unread count, the Comments tab badge's number.** TCH `f872d29d2` made the chat column's Comments tab badge and the start screen's Comments card count this viewer's unread open threads (`comment-view.mjs` `unreadBadge`, the All pages pill), while the toolbar still counted every open thread (`openCount`). The read marks live only in tracy-chat-input (`comment-reads.mjs`), so the number now comes from there and is never counted here: tracy-chat-input sends `tracy:comment-unread` `{count}` on every change (`comment-unread.mjs` `tellUnreadCount`; null until the marks are in), and a toolbar that mounts later asks once, synchronously, with `tracy:comment-unread-state` (the `tracy:turn-state` pattern; `comment-store.ts` `COMMENT_UNREAD_EVENT`, `COMMENT_UNREAD_STATE_EVENT`, `readUnreadCount`, `askUnreadCount`). `BrowserView` keeps it (`useUnreadCount`) and `CommentsButton` takes `count: number | null` instead of the comments; nothing is drawn at 0 or null (marks not in, or no chat column). Opening a thread, Mark as unread and a Delete's Undo window move it at once, because they move the chat column's count. `openCount` is removed (no reader left). No new copy. Tests: `tests/comment-store.spec.ts`, `tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx`, `tests/tracy-browser-toolbar.spec.tsx` ("Comments N" is the chat column's unread count).

`-tracy.58` (02/10/2026, TCH `fix/comment-read-on-any-open`, the product owner's decision). **No Ask Tracy to edit goes out without a saved comment: the page box's whole-page send is gone.** `sendPage` (a `tracy:comment-act` `send` with `page: true` + `text`: whole-page words to the chat, no comment made) had no way in from the UI any more: chat-input dropped the Comments tab's "Add a comment…" box on 01/10 (TCH `0e8520885`) and nothing dispatched `pageSendAct`. Removed with it: `CommentActDetail.page` (`readCommentAct` no longer reads it, so a `send` with `page: true` and no `ids` does nothing), the `'page'` `SendWhere` and `lastSendFailure` (read only by `sendPage`), and `kind: 'send'` from `CommentActFailedDetail` / `pageActFailed`. The page box's `add` (`addGeneral`, also the lost box's `addLost` / `sendLost`) is unchanged. Tests: `tests/comment-people-controller.spec.tsx` (a page `send` sends nothing; the round 6 one-tab tests now probe with `send` + ids), `tests/comment-store.spec.ts`.

`-tracy.57` (02/10/2026, TCH `fix/comment-read-on-any-open`, the product owner's decision). **A new pick's "Ask Tracy to edit" keeps the words as a comment first, so the Comments list tracks every ask.** Measured on cowork.tracy.site: "Note for team" then ⋮ Ask Tracy to edit left a comment tagged Asked Tracy → Tracy working… → Done by Tracy, while "Ask Tracy to edit" straight from the popover reached the chat and the site but kept nothing, so teammates could not see who asked Tracy to change what. `comment-controller.ts` `sendToTracy` (new pick) now runs `keepPick` — the body of "Note for team" (`addComment` calls it too): the comment is made locally, POSTed with the box's files, the popover closes and the page points again — then, once the server has numbered it, sends that comment as the Comments list's row does (`itemOf(comment, null, files)` through `sendItems`): `POST /requests` names its `commentId`, so the server files the ask under it (`sends`, `answeredAt`) and chat-input files the turn under it (`commentIds`, "Tracy working…"); `markSent` mirrors "Asked Tracy" at once. No second mechanism and no server change. Made once: a refused create gives the box back (`giveBack`) and sends nothing; a send that does not go leaves the comment as a note and says why over the page (`sendItems(…, 'view')`); the row's or the card's Ask Tracy to edit tries again, never a second comment. The box's files go to the chat as the `File`s it held (the bytes the create uploaded, not read back through their door). The pick's own lookup is still waited for at most `SEND_LOCATE_WAIT_MS` and not asked twice (`RequestItem.looked`, skipped by `locateAll`). A box that closes on a kept pick drops its earlier "could not save" (`saveError`). The edit popover's, the thread card's, "Ask Tracy to edit all (N)" (`sendSome`) and the Comments tab's page box (`sendPage`, whole-page words, still no comment) are unchanged. No new copy. Tests: `tests/comment-people-controller.spec.tsx` (the new-place popover; files; IN5-5), `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx` (a pick; the popover under a reload).

`-tracy.56` (02/10/2026, TCH `fix/sidebar-html-relative-path`). **The HTML preview opens a file whose path is relative to the session.** A file opened from a chat link carries `TracyWork/deliverables/x.html`; `encodeHtmlUrl` turned that into `/sidebar/html/<sid>/TracyWork/…`, the host read it as the absolute `/TracyWork/…` and answered `ENOENT` in the frame (cowork.tracy.site, right after the gate let seats preview at all). `api.ts` `htmlPreviewUrl` joins a relative path to the session folder before encoding — the scope's `cwd` when the caller has it, otherwise `session.cwd` from the host, the folder `fs.read` resolves the same path against — and `TextEditor` renders the frame once that URL is known. The route and its wire format are unchanged. Tests: `tests/html-preview-url.spec.ts`.

A write answered 404 drops the row quietly and reads the list again; Send first reads what changed when the last answer is older than `FRESH_MS` (5 s) (F7). `tracy:comment-status` `done`/`failed` may carry `answer` (the words after ✓ / ✗); it is kept on the comment, PATCHed to the door (TCH migration `037-site-comment-answer.sql`), read back from rows, and printed as the thread's `answer` for Tracy's line (F9). Tests: `tests/comment-controller-server.spec.tsx` (F2–F9 blocks), `comment-thread-store.spec.ts`, `comment-api.spec.ts`.

`-tracy.11` (28/09/2026): a reload of the browser tab reaches the site instead of the browser's cache. The plain rung (a page with no preview agent) assigned `frame.src = frame.src`, which replays whatever Chrome kept for that address; a site copy had once answered `/` with a 301 to its source site, so the tab showed a broken page while the site answered 200, and no reload cleared it. The frame now loads the address with a fresh `tracy_reload` nonce (`withReloadNonce`, `comment-model.ts`), and so does the rung that drops a used preview ticket. Like the ticket it lives in the iframe's `src` only: the tab's address, its record and "Copy link" stay clean, and `readReady`/`readPick` take it off what the page reports, so it never reaches `content.locate` or the agent's message. TCH's site proxy stops the 301 from being kept in the first place (`apps/tracy-web/src/bar/site-proxy.js` `forgetPermanentRedirect`); this covers browsers that already hold one. Tests: `tests/comment-model.spec.ts`, `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx`, `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx`.

A 503, a 5xx or a dropped read still retries. Before this, one idle seat page drew 24 × 403 a minute. Tests: `tests/sidebar-auto-activation.spec.tsx`, `tests/subagent-jobs-view.spec.tsx`, `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx`.

`src/client`. Only this site's own page may declare a picker — a `ready` was believed from ANY origin
the owned frame showed, so a page reached by a link inside the frame could announce one, be sent
`pick-start`, and then send `picked` with text of its own into the agent's turn while the agent held
write access to the site. The refresh watchdog's fallback reload reads today's state instead of the

doing nothing. A send voided while its lookup was awaited now says so instead of returning in silence.
And a `ready` clears `retried`, so every later expiry of the picker's ~15-minute cookie recovers, not
only the first.

Base: upstream `omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar` tag `v0.21.1` (peer DSH `^0.1.7-rc.1`), merged into
Tracy's `0.18.1-tracy.9` on 26/09/2026. Tracy runs it on its dsh fork `0.1.7-rc.2-tracy.3`.

How it was built (repeat for the next upgrade): clone upstream, branch `tracy` from the previous
base tag, rsync the fork over it (excluding `.git`, `node_modules`, `lib`) as one commit, `git merge`
the new tag, resolve, then rsync back into `vendor/tracy/dsh-better-sidebar` (again without `lib`,
which TCH builds itself). `git diff v0.21.1 tracy` in that clone shows the whole fork.

Lockstep: `package.json` `version`, `dsh.plugin.json` `version` and `SIDEBAR_SERVICE_VERSION`
(`src/client/service.ts`) move together; `tests/service.spec.ts` and `tests/manifest-consistency.spec.ts`
assert the pairs.

Known red in TCH (environment, not code): `tests/fs-operations.spec.ts` "refuses upload
directories…" (macOS `rmSync` on a dangling directory symlink) and `tests/smoke.spec.ts` "fs.read
resolves repo-relative paths…" (needs the plugin directory to be its own git repository).

## Site menu and launcher integration (0.21.1-tracy.4)

The native Browser title keeps its canonical siteKey before body mount and after reload through the existing Browser mirror. Its chevron offers accepted sites, refreshes access when opened, and reads each site's declared favicon from Tracy's seat-scoped `/api/sites/:key/favicon` door; the CMS glyph is the fallback. The menu's pointerdown is stopped before it reaches the native tab chip's drag handler, so clicking a parent row routes Live Edit through the existing page/mode deep link into the selected workspace. Team, Settings and Site changes route to their site-scoped views (Site changes replaced History in `-tracy.65`). The content heading is Live Edit; Comment/Edit mode and zoom stay intact. The host fork supplies the registry-backed plus launcher and collision-aware Menu, including scrolling site lists and submenu keyboard entry/return. Tests: `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx`, `tests/browser-mode.spec.tsx`, native surface/guide tests.

## Site menu navigation (0.21.1-tracy.7)

Selecting the site already mounted in the current browser window stays in that window: an already visible destination closes the menu without navigation, while another destination opens or focuses its native right Sidebar tab in the current session. Selecting another site opens its site-scoped deep link in a new browser tab with no source session id, preserving the first site’s UI and CWD. The named URL mount decides the current workspace; the shared last-site cookie does not.

The redundant Live Edit heading above the browser controls is removed; the siteKey tab and the site menu retain their labels.

## Surviving patches

- **P1 workspace fence, no off switch** — `fenceEnabledOf()` always true and `settings.update`
  refuses `workspaceFence: false` (`src/index.ts`); no toggle in `builtins/tabs.tsx`;
  `FenceErrorNotice.tsx` has no "turn off" button; the `workspaceFence === false` bypass in
  `changes/GitLens.tsx` is removed.
- **P2 fence cwd fail-closed** — `sessionCwdOf` (`src/index.ts`): session header, else the
  persistence read handle's header (no event log read); a client cwd only inside that workspace
  (`workspaceCwd`, `src/path-security.ts`); no `process.cwd()` fallback. Specs:
  `tests/route-cwd-fence.spec.ts`, `tests/smoke.spec.ts`.
- **P4 `tracy:browser`** — Tracy's site preview as a page kind of DSH's native right Sidebar
  (`src/client/BrowserView.tsx`, `builtins/tracy-browser.tsx`, `src/client/browser.ts`): frame
  fallback through `/sidebar/frame` when the probe (`browser.probe` route, `src/browser-probe.ts`)
  says the site refuses framing, no sandbox for a Tracy site (`siteDomain` from `/api/config`),
  follows the record's address, reload by nonce with the preview agent's in-place `style` refresh
  (`preview-protocol.generated.ts` is GENERATED by TCH's `packages/cms/tracy-cms-preview`). Hidden
  from the native guide. Open with `openTab({ type: 'tracy:browser', url, title })`; one page per
  pane, so a second open navigates it. `native/tab-adapter.tsx` carries a first open's `url` seed
  into `meta.url`. Spec: `tests/tracy-browser.spec.tsx`.
- **P5 frame route + `sidebarFrame`** — `/sidebar/frame` (`src/frame-proxy.ts`) and the host
  service `sidebarFrame.useCredentials` (`src/index.ts`, `src/context-types.ts`).
- **P7 page base** — `dshUrl`/`dshRoot` (`src/client/page-base.ts`) for every API, upload, file,
  HTML-preview, chunk, `ws/fs-watch` and `ws/agent-opens` URL (`api.ts`, `chunk-loader.ts`, `use-dir-watch.ts`,
  `sidebar/use-host-feeds.ts`, `TextEditor.tsx`, `changes/DiffPane.tsx`). `ws/agent-opens` came with upstream 0.21.x and
  missed the patch until 0.21.1-tracy.3 (behind Tracy's mount it got 403 and the agent's opens never reached the page);
  `tests/page-base.spec.ts` now fails on any root-absolute `/sidebar/` URL literal in `src/client`.
- **P9 service seams** — `DiffView` (+ `expandAll` in `diff/DiffFiles.tsx`), feature `diffView`;
  `reloadTab(tabId, mode)` through the native surface's record (or the store for a bottom tab) and
  `openTabsOf(type)` to find native ids, feature `reloadTab`. Spec: `tests/tracy-service.spec.ts`.
- **P12 main session** — `src/client/main-session.ts` (`current` or `retainedBy.mainView`) for the
  side chat's "save as session" switch and the mention scope.
- **P13 composer slot** — `conversation-draft.ts` scopes the composer lookup to
  `findConversationSlot()` (`center-column.ts`).
- **P14 no bottom toggle** — `registerBottomToggle` is not called (`src/client/index.tsx`).
- **P17 prose file mentions** — `mention-intercept.ts` + `mention-scope.ts`, wired by
  `mention-open.ts` (upstream deleted `intercept.tsx`). Spec: `tests/mention-open.spec.ts`.
- **P21 guide honours `available`** — the native guide lists a descriptor's type only while its
  `available(ctx, scope, state)` answers true for the ON-SCREEN session (`mountedSessions` + the
  list's cwd); a flip re-registers the TYPE only, the body/title slots stay
  (`src/client/native/index.ts`). `service.refreshAvailable()` (feature `refreshAvailable`) lets a
  registrant re-ask after its own lookup lands. Without it three Build plugins showed Build ×3 and
  Live site ×3 (26/09/2026). Spec: `tests/native-guide-available.spec.ts`.
- **P22 ids in an insecure context** — every client id goes through `randomId()`
  (`src/client/random-id.ts`): `crypto.randomUUID` is undefined on plain http to a non-loopback host,
  and the side chat's tab factory crashed there. Spec: `tests/random-id.spec.ts`.
- **P25 jobs routes answer one session's OWN jobs** (29/09/2026, TCH `fix/sidebar-jobs-and-titles`;
  in `0.21.1-tracy.20`, `src/jobs-routes.ts` `ownJobs`):
  `jobs.list` returns only the jobs whose `owner` is the named session, and `jobs.kill` refuses (404,
  like an unknown id) a job that session does not own. dsh's registry also hands every unowned job to
  any caller, which is why dsh-passwords refused `jobs.*` to every seat (TCH #515) — every person on a
  Tracy lane is a seat, so each Browser-tab page drew one 403 and the Tasks page never showed a job.
  With this fence dsh-passwords `2.6.6-tracy.52` opens the three routes inside a granted session. Every
  real producer (bash, subagent, workflow, terminal) sets an owner, so nothing a person started is
  lost. `SidebarJobView` gains the registry's `owner`. Spec: `tests/jobs-routes.spec.ts`.
- **P24 the Browser tab as a browser** (0.21.1-tracy.16, 29/09/2026, `BrowserView.tsx` + `sidebar.module.css`):
  `allow={BROWSER_IFRAME_ALLOW}` + `allowFullScreen` on the frame (was `allow=""`, which took fullscreen,
  clipboard and autoplay even from the unsandboxed Tracy site); `iframeSandboxFor` grants `allow-same-origin`
  to every page but the GUI's own origin (the opaque origin made every non-Tracy site behave as if cookies
  were off; `allow-top-navigation` stays withheld); a loading line (`data-loading`) from a `src` change or
  reload until the frame's `load` (an agent's `applied` clears it only for a style swap — anything else
  reloads the page); `followPage`: a `ready` from the frame's own window naming an address on the origin
  it sent from moves the bar, the record, the history and the deep link without touching the frame
  (`pageAddress`/`shown`; the first document after a navigation is a redirect and REPLACES the entry;
  Back/Forward/Enter go through `loadAgain`, which never replays a single-use ticket); a Tracy site is
  never probed (owner-only route, verdict known from the proxy's `frame-ancestors`). Spec:
  `tests/tracy-browser-native.spec.tsx`.
- **P23 Edit (comment-to-edit) mode in `tracy:browser`** (0.21.1-tracy.2 → -tracy.3 on 27/09/2026 evening: `-tracy.2` on `develop` is the first cut of P23; `-tracy.3` adds the mode bar, per-tab persistence, deep links on both addresses and Copy link) — a mode bar, the
  pin and a popover over the site preview, cut down on 27/09 pm to what the person needs:
  a text box ("What should change here?"), ⌘/Ctrl + ↵, **Send to Tracy** and close (X; Esc goes to Interactive). The
  page draws the outline itself (dashed while pointing, solid once picked); the tab draws no hover
  label, no provenance, no level walking. Drawing:
  `packages/dev/tracy-design/src/mockups/browser-comment.mock.stories.tsx`. `content.locate` is
  asked ONCE per pick in the background; Send waits for it at most 3 s, then sends `locate: null`
  (the agent's tool guidance has it call `content.locate` itself). The answer rides to the chat
  untouched; the chat chip shows plain words only (`plainLabel`: the record's name when resolved,
  else a quote of the element's text, an image's alt or file name). Pure rules in
  `src/client/comment-model.ts`, the three calls (tracy-web's `POST /api/sites/:key/preview-ticket`
  and `…/apply {action:'content.locate'}`, the `tracy:comment-send` window event) in
  `comment-client.ts`, state in `comment-controller.ts`, drawing in `CommentLayer.tsx` + the
  `comment*` / `mode*` classes of `sidebar.module.css`, the `edit*` copy keys in every dictionary. The
  preview ticket goes into the iframe `src` ONLY (never `meta.url`, the bar or the history).
  Specs: `tests/comment-model.spec.ts`, `tests/comment-client.spec.ts`,
  `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx`.
  **Mode bar (27/09 pm, third pass — like Claude Design):** the Comment button left the bar;
  its right end (after Go and Open in browser) carries a zoom select (50–200 %, default 100 %) and
  a segmented Interactive (pointer icon) | Edit (pencil + "Edit"). The word "Comment" is off the
  screen and the copy keys are `edit*` (plus `modeInteractive`, `modeInteractiveTitle`,
  `browserMode`, `browserZoom`). Mode and zoom are the TAB's: `meta.mode` / `meta.zoom` in the tab
  record, mirrored to localStorage under the tab id because the native Sidebar keeps no `meta`
  across a page reload (`src/client/browser-mode.ts`). In Edit every fresh `ready` naming `pick`
  re-arms picking; a new address, a reload or "Send to Tracy" does not leave Edit; Esc (tab or
  page) goes to Interactive; the popover's X drops the pick and points again. A deep link's
  `?mode=edit|interactive` sets the mode and is stripped before the ticket request, the iframe,
  the bar, the record and the history; "Open in browser" never carries it. Zoom scales only the
  framed page (`transform: scale()` from the top centre, not CSS `zoom` — see `frameZoomStyle`);
  the pin/popover are placed through the same transform (`scaleRect`). Spec:
  `tests/browser-mode.spec.tsx`.
  **Real browser address (27/09 evening):** the view dispatches `tracy:browser-view`
  (`BROWSER_VIEW_EVENT`, detail `{tabId, sessionId, siteKey, url, mode}`; `url: null` = the view
  went) on mount and on every change of page or mode; `@tracy/dsh-site-tabs` mirrors it into the dsh
  page's `?open=browser&page=&mode=` and reads that link on load. The mode bar ends with an
  icon-only "Copy link" (Tracy site page in a site workspace only) copying `siteDeepLink` —
  `<origin>/<siteKey>/?open=browser&page=<path>&mode=<mode>`, no session id — through
  `navigator.clipboard` with an `execCommand('copy')` fallback (strings `browserCopyLink`,
  `browserLinkCopied`, `browserLinkCopyFailed`).
  **Tickets only for Tracy sites (27/09 night, still `-tracy.3`, unreleased):** the bounded
  recovery asked a ticket and reloaded whatever the tab showed, so a tab in Edit moved to an
  imported site's own domain loaded `https://<domain>/?tracy_preview=pv1…` (measured on the stand,
  TCH `tasks/evidence/comment-to-edit/import-findings.md`). One predicate (`ticketable` in
  `comment-controller.ts`: site workspace, domains known, Tracy site) now gates the first load, the
  recovery's start and its reload. Spec: the last case of `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx`.
  **Robustness (28/09, rides with the unreleased `-tracy.4`):** (a) Edit turned on over a page that loaded
  with no picker (the cookie lapsed in Interactive, where no load is watched) starts the recovery's one
  reload with a fresh ticket (`press-silent`, `silenceOf` in `comment-model.ts`; inside the
  `READY_ECHO_MS` window it is watched instead, because a page's first `ready` can be credited to the
  blank frame's load); (b) a new document of the SAME page (the agent's turn end reloads it) keeps
  the open pick — text, lookup, a send on its way — and is not armed under the popover; only a new
  address, Esc or X drops it; a send failure the popover can no longer show is said over the page
  (`notice`, `.commentNotice`); (c) the pick's `content.locate` belongs to the pick (id + document,
  `sameElement`), one in flight, and an `incomplete` or missing answer is asked again at Send
  (`src/client/pick-lookup.ts`); (d) `locateElement` gives up after `LOCATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s).
  Specs: `tests/pick-lookup.spec.ts`, new cases in `tests/comment-model.spec.ts`,
  `tests/comment-client.spec.ts` and `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx` (which now stubs dsh's
  `Pill`/`Menu` like its icons, so it runs on a machine with two React copies).
  **The page's address and box (28/09, rides with the unreleased `-tracy.5`; needs TCH's preview runtime 4):**
  (e) the page now sends its own `url` on `ready` (to the vouched origin only), `pick-hover` and
  `picked`, and the controller names the pick's page by it for `content.locate` and the chat turn,
  the address bar only when none came — after a link followed inside the frame the bar still shows
  the page the tab opened, and a new document of ANOTHER page now drops an open pick; (f) while an
  element stays picked the page sends `picked` again with `moved: true` as it scrolls or resizes (at
  most once per frame): the popover and pin follow, and such a box never opens a pick (`readPick`
  `moved`; `clearPick` forgets the pick at once, so a box handled before the next render cannot
  bring it back). Specs: new cases in `tests/comment-model.spec.ts` and
  `tests/tracy-browser-comment.spec.tsx` ("the page scrolls under the popover", "a link followed
  inside the frame").
  **Many comments, one send — the model (28/09, stage 3 piece F1, unreleased; version NOT bumped —
  the integrator picks the `-tracy.N`; needs TCH's preview runtime 5 for the multi-pin flow):** a page
  whose `ready` names `track` gets numbered comments instead of the single pick; a page naming only
  `pick` keeps everything above byte for byte (`foot: 'single'`). New `src/client/comment-store.ts`
  (pure): the `Comment`/`CommentStore` record of TCH contract H2 and its reducer (`add`, `save`,
  `remove`, `clear`, `markSent`, `markStatus`, `markLost`/`markFound`, `setLocate`, `sweepDone`;
  numbers never reused; `MAX_COMMENTS` 12, the 13th refused `full`; empty words never stored), the
  restore that trusts nothing (version, site, ≤ 12, each field; `sent|working` back as `sent`), the
  `pick-track`/`pick-rect`/`pick-lost` wire (H1, through the generated `previewTrackMessage`), the
  `tracy:comment-send` v2 detail (N ≥ 2; one comment still goes as v1) and `tracy:comment-status`
  (H3). `browser-mode.ts`: `canonicalPageUrl` (H4: Tracy params and fragment off), the mirror's
  `comments` (`saveViewComments`) and `commentStoreOf` (`meta.comments`, even empty, beats the
  mirror). `comment-controller.ts` runs it (state block at its top: `comments`, `pageComments`,
  `rects`, `foot`, `active`, `discardPrompt`, `pendingCount`, `pagesSummary`, `refused`, `sending`, and
  `addAnother`/`openComment`/`saveActive`/`removeComment`/`clearAll`/`sendAll`/`escape`/`keepEditing`/
  `discard`); `BrowserView` keeps the store in `meta.comments` + the mirror. `CommentLayer.tsx` only
  routes Esc through `escape` (one step per press, page or parent) and ⌘⇧↵ to `addAnother`; the
  drawing of pins, strip, edit popover and sheet is the next piece. New copy key `editFailedTooLong`
  (21 dictionaries). Specs: `tests/comment-store.spec.ts`, `tests/comment-persist.spec.ts`,
  `tests/comment-controller-multi.spec.tsx`, `tests/tracy-browser-multi-pin.spec.tsx`.
  **Fix round 1 from the stand E2E (29/09, `tasks/evidence/comment-multi-pin/stand-e2e.md` H1, M1, L-a):**
  on a `track` page every send is v2, one comment included (a lone v1 lost the tab's number, so the pin
  ended yellow or stuck in sent); a new pick or a new batch removes every `done|failed|asked` comment of
  earlier batches at once (`sweepResolved`); a comment `sent`/`working` for `STUCK_MS` (10 min, from the
  new `sentAt`) becomes `asked` (`expireStuck`, also on mount; a kept one without `sentAt` counts as
  stuck); a `failed` waits `FAILED_SETTLE_MS` (1.5 s) and a later `working`/`done` for the same number
  cancels it, so a retried refusal never flashes red.
  **Round 2 (29/09, V2-L0/V2-L1):** `locateElement` asks nothing when the element has no words, no image
  and no marks (`hasLocateQuery`; the door answered 400 `LOCATE_BAD_QUERY`) — the comment goes with
  `locate: null`; `sweepResolved` removes finished comments only of batches with no comment still
  `sent`/`working`, so a refusal the agent is about to retry keeps its pin until the turn settles.
- **P19 lockstep** — see above. The optional peer `@huanlin/dsh-plugin-better-locale` is
  `>=0.1.0 || >=0.3.0-tracy.1` so Tracy's fork satisfies it.

Dropped at 0.21.1 (upstream removed the feature, or the native Sidebar replaces it): P3 terminal via
`ctx.subprocess`, P6 `browser_read`/`browser_reload`, P8 seed tabs / open by default (the native
column starts collapsed per session), P9 tab links / `group` / `reveal` / `setPanelOpen`, P10 title
fallback, P11 blank-session forget, P15 open-resource shadow, P16/P18 turn-tail row, P20 files entry.
Session format V4 (`plugin:dsh-better-sidebar` source kind) and `jobs.list` are upstream's own
(its owner fence is P25).
